\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آبیاری} \fa{کردن} (âbyâri kardan)}{آبیاری کردن (âbyâri kardan)}]{\fa{آبیاری} \fa{کردن} (âbyâri kardan) — to water (plants)}

\label{lesson:FA-C539-abyari-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to heat, then the Persian for to get cold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آبیاری} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{آبیاری} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{âbyâri kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to water (plants)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{عصرها} \fa{گلها} \fa{را} \fa{آبیاری} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedaram 'asrhâ golhâ râ âbyâri mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father waters the flowers in the afternoons.
\end{quote}

\emph{âbyâri} 'irrigation' + \emph{kardan}. In speech also \emph{âb dâdan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âbyâri} is built on native \emph{âb}, 'water', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian (EtymDB); the rest is usually explained as \emph{yâri}, 'help': helping with water. \emph{kardan} is inherited.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âbyâri kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âbyâri kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{âbyâri kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to heat, then the Persian for to get cold, then say \emph{âbyâri kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{چمن} \fa{زدن} (chaman zadan)}{چمن زدن (chaman zadan)}]{\fa{چمن} \fa{زدن} (chaman zadan) — to mow the lawn}

\label{lesson:FA-C539-chaman-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to get cold, then the Persian for to water.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{چمن} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{چمن} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{chaman zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to mow the lawn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{همسایه} \fa{ما} \fa{هر} \fa{هفته} \fa{چمن} \fa{میزند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hamsâye-ye mâ har hafte chaman mizanad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our neighbour mows the lawn every week.
\end{quote}

\emph{chaman} 'lawn, grass' + \emph{zadan} 'to strike'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{chaman} is the Persian word for a lawn; EtymDB lists it beside \emph{chamidan}, 'to stroll' (EtymDB), but its origin is not settled. \emph{zadan}, 'to strike', is inherited.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chaman zadan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chaman zadan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{chaman zadan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to get cold, then the Persian for to water, then say \emph{chaman zadan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{حیوان} \fa{خانگی} (heyvân-e khânegi)}{حیوان خانگی (heyvân-e khânegi)}]{\fa{حیوان} \fa{خانگی} (heyvân-e khânegi) — a pet}

\label{lesson:FA-C539-heyvan-e-khanegi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to water, then the Persian for to mow the lawn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{حیوان} \fa{خانگی}}
\textbf{\fa{حیوان} \fa{خانگی}} (\emph{heyvân-e khânegi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a pet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ما} \fa{یک} \fa{گربه} \fa{به} \fa{عنوان} \fa{حیوان} \fa{خانگی} \fa{داریم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâ yek gorbe be 'onvân-e heyvân-e khânegi dârim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We have a cat as a pet.
\end{quote}

\emph{heyvân} 'animal' + \emph{khânegi} 'of the home'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{heyvân-e khânegi} is built in Persian on \emph{heyvân}, from Arabic \emph{ḥayawān}, 'animal' (EtymDB), and \emph{khânegi}, 'of the home', from native \emph{khâne}, 'house'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{heyvân-e khânegi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{heyvân-e khânegi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to water, then the Persian for to mow the lawn, then say \emph{heyvân-e khânegi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{غذا} \fa{دادن} (ghazâ dâdan)}{غذا دادن (ghazâ dâdan)}]{\fa{غذا} \fa{دادن} (ghazâ dâdan) — to feed}

\label{lesson:FA-C539-ghaza-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to mow the lawn, then the Persian for a pet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{غذا} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{غذا} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{ghazâ dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to feed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دخترم} \fa{هر} \fa{صبح} \fa{به} \fa{ماهیها} \fa{غذا} \fa{میدهد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dokhtaram har sobh be mâhihâ ghazâ midahad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My daughter feeds the fish every morning.
\end{quote}

\emph{be kasi ghazâ dâdan}; \emph{ghazâ} 'food' + \emph{dâdan} 'to give'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ghazâ} comes from Arabic \emph{ġiḏāʾ}, 'nourishment, food' (EtymDB). \emph{dâdan}, 'to give', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghazâ dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ghazâ dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to mow the lawn, then the Persian for a pet, then say \emph{ghazâ dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دورهمی} (dowrehami)}{دورهمی (dowrehami)}]{\fa{دورهمی} (dowrehami) — a get-together (of family or friends)}

\label{lesson:FA-C539-dowrehami}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a pet, then the Persian for to feed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دورهمی}}
\textbf{\fa{دورهمی}} (\emph{dowrehami}) — \textquotedblleft{}a get-together (of family or friends)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آخر} \fa{هفته} \fa{ها} \fa{در} \fa{خانه} \fa{مادربزرگ} \fa{دورهمی} \fa{داریم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{âkhar-e haftehâ dar khâne-ye mâdarbozorg dowrehami dârim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At weekends we have a get-together at grandmother's house.
\end{quote}

Colloquial: \emph{dowr-e ham} 'around each other' + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dowrehami} is built in Persian on \emph{dowr}, 'circle, round', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{dawr}, and native \emph{ham}, 'together', with \emph{-i}: sitting round together. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dowrehami}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dowrehami}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dowrehami}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a pet, then the Persian for to feed, then say \emph{dowrehami} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
